_why: plex.tv stores share-filter strings VERBATIM and hands them straight back — there is no
server-side normalization of either separator. Measured by writing each form to a real
account's filterMovies via PUT /api/users/{id} (params=, exactly as plextv.update_user_filters
does) and reading it back from GET /api/users. The account's original value was snapshotted
first and restored afterwards, verified byte-identical.
The consequence is the whole of issue #77: the shape Shortlist reads is whichever writer last
touched that account, so all four of these reach parse_filter. Splitting only on '|' and ','
mis-parsed the Plex Web form into ONE condition whose field swallowed the allow clause, which
made the existing exclude clause invisible and caused a merge to append a second one.
Note the httpx params= layer round-trips cleanly: '%' in a value goes out as '%25' and comes
back as '%', so a %2C-joined value survives as %2C rather than double-encoding.

known_writers.plex_web: '&' between conditions, values URL-encoded (per issue #77's devtools capture)
known_writers.shortlist: '|' between conditions, values joined with a plain comma

exclude_only_accounts_observed._note: All 48 accounts on the recording server, written only ever by Shortlist, came back plain and single-clause — no '&', no '|', no percent-encoding, and no sign of double-encoding.
